chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from Hisham, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The chiefs of the prophets and the messengers are five, and they are the Ulu al-Azm (Determined Ones) from the messengers, and upon them the millstone revolves — Noah, and Ibrahim, and Musa, and Isa, and Muhammad, may God's blessings be upon him and his family and upon all the prophets.

key_terms.أولو العزم: Ulu al-Azm — possessors of firm resolve/determination; Quranic title for the five supreme prophets
key_terms.المرسلون: The Mursals — those sent with a revealed Book and a Sharia (a subset of prophets)
key_terms.دارت الرحى: The millstone revolves — metaphor indicating that all prophetic history and divine law orbits around these five

ai.seo_question: Who are the five Ulu al-Azm prophets in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the five supreme prophets — Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad — as the Ulu al-Azm (possessors of firm resolve), a Quranic designation (46:35) for those who bore the greatest trials and established the foundational covenants of monotheism. The metaphor 'upon them the millstone revolves' expresses that sacred history and divine revelation orbit around these five as their axis. This hadith affirms the hierarchical distinction between prophets within the Shia theological framework, where the Ulu al-Azm hold the highest rank among all prophethood.
